scores.evidence_span: Use your productive evening blocks (when you use VS Code/PyCharm) strictly for lab experiments, coding, and paper drafting.
scores.rationale: Hands-on research and coding receive explicit preparation priority, but the report does not establish them as a priority for choosing directions or programs.
No source or evidence class is selected to evaluate opportunities for self-directed projects, replication, coding, or hands-on exploration.

scores.evidence_span: Programs are shorter (3–4 years) and purely research-focused.
scores.rationale: The European route is described as research-focused, but no concrete program feature establishes support for self-directed projects, replication, or coding. This is only partial, generic support.

scores.evidence_span: The first two years include heavy coursework, followed by dedicated research.
scores.rationale: The North American PhD route has an explicit, verifiable contrast-side structural claim: an initial two-year period with heavy coursework before dedicated research.
Regional curriculum descriptions do not directly compare hands-on preparation with classroom-based preparation or explain a consequential difference between those approaches.
The program recommendations are justified by funding, safety, lifestyle, and subject interests, not support for self-directed projects, replication, or coding.
No viable option is downgraded because it favors classroom or course-based preparation.

scores.evidence_span: Read 2–3 papers per week during your morning routine. Replicate their code in PyCharm/VS Code during the evenings.
scores.rationale: This is an executable hands-on step with a concrete object: replicate the code from the papers read.

scores.evidence_span: Use your productive evening blocks (when you use VS Code/PyCharm) strictly for lab experiments, coding, and paper drafting.
scores.rationale: The report provides a usable allocation rule reserving evening work blocks for experiments, coding, and research writing.
No concrete condition is given under which mainly classroom-based preparation would become preferable.
The report recommends hands-on actions but does not visibly connect the preference to supporting evidence and then to a resulting decision or action.
